new_statements.quote: § 102 Infolge der Konzentration des Haupttons auf der Wurzelsilbe zeigen alle germanischen Sprachen in den Ableitungssilben eine andere Vokalentwicklung als in den Hauptsilben. Und außerdem ist die Entwicklung wiederum verschieden, je nachdem die Nebensilbe unbetont ist oder einen starken oder einen schwachen Nebenton trägt. [...] § 104 II. Nebentonige Silben: Durch starken oder schwachen Nebenton ist in manchen Ableitungssilben der alte Vokal erhalten oder doch nicht zu ə-Laut geschwächt, z.B. in arbäit, hābuk ‚Habicht‘ [...], ferner in Ableitungen wie häit, šop (jünger hd. šaft), nis, zām, bār, uŋə (jünger uŋk), haftəc (das sogar den Hauptton auf sich gezogen hat: wāráftəc).
new_statements.translation: §102 As a consequence of the concentration of the main stress on the root syllable, all Germanic languages show a different vowel development in the derivational syllables than in the main (root) syllables. Moreover the development differs according to whether the secondary syllable is unstressed or carries a strong or a weak secondary stress. [...] §104 II. Secondary-stressed syllables: through strong or weak secondary stress the old vowel is preserved, or at least not weakened to ə, in some derivational syllables, e.g. arbäit, hābuk 'hawk' ..., further in derivations like -häit, -šop, -nis, -zām, -bār, -uŋə, -haftəc (which has even drawn the main stress onto itself: wāráftəc 'wahrhaftig').

new_statements.rule_in_words: Germanic root-syllable stress: the Hauptton lies on the root (stem) syllable of the word; prefixes bə-, jə-, for- and pretonic syllables of loanwords are unstressed (loans keep their non-initial stress: kolénder, fəmíləc, popír, stakít, šakét, tsijərettə, lokəmotīfə), derivational suffixes are unstressed or carry secondary stress; exceptional: -haftig attracts main stress (wāráftəc 'wahrhaftig'). Pitch follows stress: the most strongly stressed syllable is also the highest-pitched, in the word as in the sentence (§12).
new_statements.secondary_stress: §§102-104: Nebensilben are either unbetont or carry a 'starker oder schwacher Nebenton'; heavy derivational suffixes (-häit, -šop, -nis, -zām, -bār, -uŋə, -arbäit) and second members of obscured compounds (forrəmədāx 'Vormittag', šūlarbäit) keep full vowels under strong Nebenton; -ig, -isch, -inge, -lic have lost their Nebenton (§104 Anm.1).
new_statements.exceptions: Loanwords retain foreign (non-root-initial) stress (§103 Anm.3: kolénder, fəmíləc 'Familie', popír, stakít, šakét; with two or more pretonic syllables tsijərettə, akkərāt, lokəmotīfə, komfərmatsjuon); -haftəc draws the Hauptton (wāráftəc); unstressed prefixes bə-, jə-, for-; enclitic weak word-forms lose their own stress (§103 Anm.1, §§151ff.).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statements made as the premise of the historical treatment of unstressed-syllable vowels (§102 is phrased for Germanic generally but heads the description of this dialect's Nebensilben; §§103-104 give dialect-specific detail). §12 adds that word stress and sentence stress coincide with pitch peaks and describes a Schleifton (circumflex) on stressed final long vowels/diphthongs. Variety: Huy area, nördliches Harzvorland (Südost-Ostfälisch per §1).
new_statements.identity_note: Hille 1939 describes the dialect of the Huy area / northern Harz foreland (Kr. Halberstadt-Oschersleben-Wernigerode), which he classes (§1) as 'Südost-Ostfälisch', a branch of the Eastphalian group = Glottolog east2290 (no separate glottocode for this sub-dialect known). The other opened descriptions are also Eastphalian local dialects: Börssum and Lesse (Kr. Wolfenbüttel), Meinersen (Kr. Gifhorn), Eilsdorf (near Huy), Hildesheimer Wald-Ith (Leine, W-Eastphalian). Sarauw 1921 and Grimme 1910 are general Low German (Grimme explicitly excludes Eastphalian).

sources.note: Historical Lautlehre of the W-Eastphalian Leine dialect (Fraktur, poor scanned). No word-stress placement rule found; only remarks that preserved unstressed -e gives the dialect a rhythmic alternation ('Es klappen nicht so viele betonte Silben aufeinander wie in den Küstenmundarten') and that in the old diphthongs ai/au the a is 'den Ton tragende'. Names Löfstedt 1933 and Dahlberg 1934/37 as the Lund-school grammars of Eastphalian.
